name: Demand-Driven Volume Rendering
definition: A GPU ray-casting technique that renders a "virtual octree" where physical data is computed on demand, driven by visibility and screen-projection size, allowing interactive rendering of terascale EM data without pre-computing a 3D multi-resolution hierarchy.
summary: Demand-Driven Volume Rendering is a GPU ray-casting technique that computes voxel data on demand via a two-level page table hierarchy, enabling interactive terascale rendering without pre-computing multi-resolution hierarchies.
